Yearly housing cost abroad (today's $): Your yearly rent, utilities, and insurance while living abroad, in today's dollars. The housing exclusion leaves out the part above 16% of the exclusion limit, up to 30% of it (more in costly cities).
Vacancy: The share of the year the rental sits empty with no tenant. A common assumption is 5%, about 2.6 weeks a year.
State: The US state you live in for tax purposes. State income taxes differ, so the state changes the taxes the plan projects each year.
Yearly payment: The total paid toward this loan each year, principal and interest. For a $300,000, 30-year mortgage at 6%, about $21,600 a year.
Cliff (years before the first vesting): The wait before any shares vest. With a 1-year cliff on a 4-year schedule, nothing vests during the first year, and the first quarter vests at once on the first anniversary.
Paid from: The account which pays this expense, such as a 529 plan for college. When the account runs out, the rest is paid from your other money.
New state: The state you move to. The plan uses that state's income tax from the move on.
Traditional IRA a year: How much you put into a traditional IRA each year; it can lower your taxable income. The 2026 limit is $7,500 ($8,600 at 50 and older).
Roth IRA a year: How much you put into a Roth IRA each year, from money already taxed; qualified withdrawals are tax-free. The 2026 limit is $7,500 ($8,600 at 50 and older).
HSA a year: How much you put into a health savings account each year. The 2026 limits are $4,400 for self-only coverage and $8,750 for family coverage.
Realize gains in the 0% capital gains ba: Each year, sells and rebuys taxable investments for gains up to the top of the 0% capital gains band, raising your cost basis at no tax. In 2026 the band ends at $49,450 of taxable income for a single filer ($98,900 for a couple).
Fill up to the bracket: Roth conversions each year fill your taxable income up to the top of the bracket you pick. A conversion is taxed now, and the money then grows tax-free.
To year: The last year of automatic Roth conversions.
Local tax: An income tax your city or county adds on top of federal and state tax. Pick New York City's brackets, a flat rate on wages, a flat rate on taxable income, or None.
Preset: A place whose local tax rate fills in for you, or Custom to enter the rate yourself.
Rate: The local tax rate, as a percent. For example, 1.5 for a flat 1.5% on wages.
Heirs' income tax rate: The income tax rate your heirs pay when they withdraw inherited pre-tax accounts (traditional IRAs and 401(k)s). Cash, homes, and taxable investments pass to heirs without income tax.
State you live in: Your state, for its income tax. The state changes the plan's tax estimates.
Yearly salary: Your yearly pay before taxes. For example, enter 85000 for $85,000 a year.
Monthly Social Security at 67 (0 to esti: Your monthly Social Security benefit if you start at full retirement age, 67 (your statement at ssa.gov/myaccount shows it). Enter 0 and the app estimates it from your salary.
Share of spending on this card: The share of the year's spending you charge to this card. For example, 60% if most purchases go on it.
Cash back: The cash back this card earns on purchases, as a percent. For example, 2 for a 2% card. Cash back is a rebate, not taxed income.
